title: Large-angle pendulum (70°)

source.credit: Rendered by Ansatz with exactly known physics (L = 0.80 m, released at 70°)

caveats: motion blur at high speed near bottom of swing

reference.basis: animated scale bar of unknown length, not a standard object

slow_motion.evidence: no on-screen text or narration indicates slow motion

subjects.description: small blue spherical bob on a black string suspended from a grey support

observation.what_happens: A blue ball on a string swings back and forth below a fixed support. It is released from a held position on the right, swings down through the center to the left and continues oscillating.

calibration.note: no ruler needed: the swing is measured as an angle

given: g = 9.807 m/s² (Earth): hold g fixed and measure the pendulum's length L in metres from its swing
reasoning: The angle oscillates ~+/-1.2 rad (~70 deg) with ~2 s period and slowly shrinking amplitude, and the path fits a circle, so it is a large-angle pendulum where sin(theta) matters. With g fixed, period sets length L~1 m, and the slow decay motivates testing no damping versus linear viscous versus quadratic aerodynamic damping.

critique.finding: The ball swings on a string of length {L} with light drag {gamma} stealing a little motion each swing. It matches the measurements down near noise.
critique.headline: Swinging ball slows gently as air resists motion
critique.why_it_won: It lets the swings shrink a little each time with linear drag, while the ideal laws keep swinging too wide and quadratic drag shrinks them the wrong way.

headline: Swinging ball slows gently as air resists motion
finding: The ball swings on a string of length 0.7999 ± 0.0021 m with light drag 0.06006 ± 0.00032 1/s stealing a little motion each swing. It matches the measurements down near noise.

eyeball.confidence: low-medium, scale bar assumed 10x10cm =1m total and background grid used for pixel scaling; period timed over ~7s clip (~300 frames at 42.9 fps)
eyeball.law_in_words: Pendulum small-angle period T = 2*pi*sqrt(L/g) gives L = g*(T/2pi)^2. L also measured geometrically: pivot to ball centre distance in image (~4 grid cells) calibrated against bottom black-white scale taken as 10 cm per division, 1 m total (~5 grid cells). Period timed frame by frame from right-maximum to right-maximum over the ~7 s clip gives T~1.8 s consistent with L~0.8 m. Damping from exponential envelope A~A0*exp(-gamma*t): peak lateral amplitude shows almost no decay over ~3-4 periods in 7 s, so gamma = (1/t)*ln(A0/A) is of order a few 1/100 per s.
